title: First Free Number After the Counting-Up Prefix
statement:
You get an array nums of positive integers. Its counting-up prefix starts with nums[0] and keeps going while each next value is exactly one more than the value before it. It stops at the first value that breaks that rule. It always has at least one element.

Let S be the sum of the counting-up prefix. Return the smallest integer x ≥ S that does not appear anywhere in nums.

examples.why: The prefix is 3, 4, 5, so S = 12. Both 12 and 13 are in the array; 14 is not. The missing 2 does not matter because it is below S.
5 is not 2 + 1, so the prefix is just [2] and S = 2. The 2, 3 later in the array do not extend it. 2 and 3 are taken, so the answer is 4.
The prefix 1, 2, 3 sums to 6, and 6 is not in the array, so S itself is the answer.

hints: Two separate jobs: find the prefix sum, then search upward from it. Do them one at a time.
The prefix ends at the first i where nums[i] !== nums[i − 1] + 1. Values after that are only used as the set of taken numbers.
Searching the array for every candidate is slow when many numbers in a row are taken. Put all values in a hash set first, then step x up from S until it is not in the set.

explain.intuition:
The prefix part is a short scan: add values while each one is the previous plus one, and stop at the first break. After that, the array matters only as a set of taken numbers.

Then walk x = S, S + 1, … until you find a free number. Each check must be O(1), so build a hash set first. The walk takes at most n + 1 steps, because only n numbers can be taken. Searching the raw array instead turns each check into O(n), and the whole thing into O(n²).
steps: Set S = nums[0]. For i = 1, 2, …, while nums[i] === nums[i − 1] + 1, add nums[i] to S; stop at the first break.
Put every value of nums into a set.
Start at x = S and increase it while x is in the set.
pitfalls: Continuing the prefix past a break. In [2, 5, 2, 3] the prefix is only [2].
Looking for the smallest missing number overall, instead of the smallest one that is at least S.
Using nums.includes(x) in the loop: O(n) per check, O(n²) when a long block of numbers is taken.

solutions.title: Search the array for each candidate
solutions.idea: Compute S, then test x = S, S+1, … by scanning the whole array each time.
solutions.py:
class Solution:
    def firstFreeAfterPrefix(self, nums: List[int]) -> int:
        s = nums[0]
        i = 1
        while i < len(nums) and nums[i] == nums[i - 1] + 1:
            s += nums[i]
            i += 1
        x = s
        while x in nums:  # list membership: O(n) each time
            x += 1
        return x

solutions.title: Prefix sum, then a hash set
solutions.idea: Same walk, but every membership check is O(1) because the values sit in a set.

followups: Answer many queries "smallest free number ≥ q" on the same array. What would you precompute?
Values can now be removed and added between queries. Which structure keeps each query fast?
